scope: Uniqueness of the reduced inverse identifies the residue (1 + N − v) mod N with the reference circuit’s Step-5 cleanup constant selected by bounded search.
Squaring a reduced multiplier and its inverse together emits exactly the reference modular-exponentiation stages. Their integer constants require at most 162(w+1)² Boolean gates per exponent control.

Shor §3. From the input modulus and a coprime base, Euclidean inversion and repeated modular squaring produce every controlled multiplier and cleanup residue for the reference clock. The emitted modular-exponentiation gate tree is equal to ForShor’s specification, with at most 624(w+1)³ Boolean gates for generating the integer constants at modulus width w. Gate lowering and finite-precision evaluation of phase entries require separate bounds.
